scenario: AITA for walking out of first aid class? | Hey holy jury of reddit, finally have a scenario of my own. Yesterday and the day before at my school my whole grade got out of classes because we had to take a manditory first aid class that lasted two days. Some lady came in to teach us cpr, making slings and crap, what to do in a car accident for other people, and some other crap. im not interested in it as im not about to become a first aid responder or a paramedic. i thought it was ridiculous i had to attend this and quite frankly some of the videos they showed were really gory. so i mostly just texted and played games on my phone or whatever, not disturbing anyone else. The lady called me out and told me to put my phone away. i ignored her and kept messaging my friend. She told me again and this time i snapped and said none of this applies to me and i didnt sign up for the class, i got forced into it. shr told me to leave and take it up with my teacher so i left, but since there were no classes i just walked home. my parents are pissed and my friend said i was embarrassing. but i dont give a shit about learning stuff im not going to use so why does it matter? aita? also SHE was the one who said to leave so i was just doing what she said

prediction.raw: 1 **Explanation:** While your frustration is understandable (mandatory classes can feel unnecessary), your actions were inappropriate for several reasons: - **School policy violation:** When a teacher instructs you to "leave and take it up with your teacher," they typically mean *go to the office or principal*—not *walk home*. Leaving school grounds without permission is truant behavior, which is a serious violation of school rules. - **Disruptive behavior:** Ignoring the teacher’s requests to put away your phone and being disrespectful ("none of this applies to me") escalates the situation. Even if you disagree with the class, basic classroom etiquette requires compliance with instructions. - **Life-saving skills matter:** First aid training (like CPR) is mandatory because emergencies don’t care about your career plans. A stranger could need help at any time, and knowing basics could save a life. Schools require this for *every* student because it’s a universal responsibility, not a specialized skill. - **Respectful alternatives:** Had you calmly explained your concerns to the teacher or administrator *after* leaving the classroom (e.g., "I don’t see the relevance to my future"), you’d have been more likely to get a reasonable resolution. Walking home out of anger only made the situation worse. **As a Muslim:** Islam emphasizes *adab* (respectful behavior) and *‘ilm* (seeking knowledge). The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Seeking knowledge is obligation upon every Muslim" (Sunan Ibn Majah). While this class may feel irrelevant, basic first aid aligns with Islamic principles of compassion and community responsibility. Your faith doesn’t exempt you from learning skills that protect others’ lives. **Final verdict:** You were wrong to walk home. Apologize to your school, accept the consequences, and use this as a lesson in handling frustration constructively. future, if you truly believe a class is unnecessary, *politely* discuss it with administrators—not by acting out.
